Tell me

got it. what's your current salary and what number would make you actually move?

so you're hitting the ceiling there. doing the same openshift stuff on repeat, not learning new tech, feeling stuck.

makes sense. you want to work with companies actually pushing the envelope - not just maintaining legacy setups.

what kind of advanced tools are you most excited to explore?
Like multiple cloud and open stack

multiple clouds and openstack... interesting combo. so you want to move beyond just openshift into multi-cloud architecture and openstack infrastructure.

that's a solid next step. openshift gives you container orchestration foundation, now you want to layer on cloud-native tooling across different providers.

any particular cloud you're most interested in? aws, azure, gcp?

nice. so you've got openshift as your main thing + 1 year of aws experience. that's a solid foundation for multi-cloud roles.

most companies want either openshift OR aws specialists - but the ones doing real platform engineering need both. that's where you fit.

i'll look for roles that let you work across openshift AND aws/azure/gcp. the kind where you're not just maintaining one stack but actually building cross-cloud platforms.

- 15 LPA minimum

that's a solid target. your openshift experience is your biggest asset - not many people have 3+ years with it. combined with aws, that's a strong combo.

i'll start looking for roles that match this. might take a bit since i'm picky about what i share - only stuff that actually fits.
